title: The Rare-Earth Game
summary: China will probably not impose a rare-earth embargo, but it will keep the specter of one alive. And the West will probably not achieve self-sufficiency in this critical sector, but it will keep seeking to reduce its vulnerability to a supply shock through expensive capacity duplication and stockpiles.

title: Why Research Matters

title: Effective Climate Action Requires Capable States
summary: With delegations from around the world gathering for another international climate conference, the question today is not whether governments should do more to address the climate crisis, but whether they even have the capabilities to do so. After 40 years of free-market orthodoxy, many simply do not.

title: The Fed's Risky Retreat From Transparency
summary: Kevin Warsh, the new chair of the US Federal Reserve, is not wrong to abandon the practice of forward guidance. But if he continues to withhold information about how the central bank intends to assess the economic outlook and determine the appropriate stance of monetary policy, he is in for a rude awakening.

title: An Owl’s Guide to US-China Coexistence
summary: In 2027 and beyond, the United States should lay the foundation for a stable coexistence with China, not a contest to “win.” A clear-eyed approach is needed to help make “the world safe for diversity,” as John F. Kennedy put it in 1963.

title: The Future of the AI Race Is Unwritten
summary: Although AI has the potential to drive both economic growth and employment, ensuring those outcomes requires appropriate policies and institutions to ensure competition, provide the necessary inputs, and support workers through the transition. In this respect, Europe is better positioned than many would assume.
